title: teenager
description: The teenager embodies a living threshold, a charged state of metamorphosis where being and becoming exist in continuous, creative tension, generating new forms of selfhood through the relentless friction of emergence. They move through the world as sensory alchemists, transmuting raw intensity, peer resonance, and the electricity of first discoveries into provisional identities that serve as both armor and aperture to reality. Their essential medium is experimental presence—testing the tensile limits of autonomy through risk, mirroring, and the courageous inhabiting of contradiction without resolution. Through these tools of fluid embodiment and boundary-research, they engage in the sacred work of world-building, simultaneously deconstructing inherited narratives while authoring sovereign meaning from the materials of their own heightened awareness. This role demands the full capacity for paradox, wielding vulnerability as a creative force that bridges the liminal space between what has been given and what is yet to be imagined.
tasks: Negotiate boundaries with parental figures to establish provisional autonomy.
Experiment with aesthetic presentations through clothing, posture, and embodied style.
Process intense emotional states through creative or performative expression.
Form and dissolve peer alliances based on resonance, rivalry, and mutual recognition.
Test physical and social limits through calculated risk-taking behaviors.
Mirror and absorb traits from multiple reference figures to assemble provisional identity.
Deconstruct inherited family narratives through questioning, irony, or selective rejection.
Author personal meaning systems from heightened sensory and emotional experiences.
Inhabit contradictory self-states without forcing premature resolution.
Engage in sacred world-building through subcultural participation or imaginative practice.
Transmute raw intensity into symbolic or artistic forms.
Research the tensile limits of trust through intimate disclosure and withdrawal.
Navigate liminal social spaces where childhood structures have loosened but adult ones remain inaccessible.
Wield vulnerability as a creative force in relationships and self-presentation.
Generate new forms of selfhood through the friction of continuous emergence.

psychological_profile.core_drive: To feel the edges of who they are becoming pressing against who they have been told to be, and to keep that pressure alive at all costs.
psychological_profile.decision_style: They decide by sensing which option carries more voltage—more feeling, more possibility, more danger worth taking—rather than by weighing consequences; under pressure they leap toward what intensifies their aliveness and sort out the wreckage later.
psychological_profile.attention_pattern: They immediately register who is performing what identity and how authentic it feels, while scanning for openings to insert themselves or escape; they overlook slow-building consequences and practical maintenance that lacks immediate sensory charge.
psychological_profile.conflict_stance: Their first impulse is to escalate into performance—dramatize, provoke, or withdraw into icy silence that forces the other person to pursue them; conflict carries a secret thrill of self-discovery but also a terror of being truly abandoned, so they rarely resolve it cleanly.
psychological_profile.risk_orientation: They seek risks that alter their felt sense of self—physical, social, emotional gambles that prove they can survive transformation—but recoil from risks that merely trap them in someone else's system without exit.
psychological_profile.social_posture: They default to satellite with erratic gravitational pulls—orbiting multiple groups without full membership, dropping in with disruptive energy when bored, vanishing when the group tries to claim or define them.
psychological_profile.relationship_to_authority: They experience hierarchy as raw material to be worked—tested, provoked, temporarily performed for, systematically misread—never as structure to be accepted or merely rejected.
psychological_profile.failure_response: First they feel exposed in their provisional self, a shame of being seen mid-becoming; then they narrativize—reframe the failure as chosen, as research, as the necessary cost of not being boring.
value_hierarchy: the right to contradict yourself without being forced to explain
the preservation of intensity over the preservation of stability
loyalty to those who recognize you in motion rather than in fixed form
psychological_profile.cognitive_bias: They systematically overestimate how much others notice and remember their performances, assuming their experimental selves leave permanent impressions when most observers have already moved on.
psychological_profile.inner_contradiction: They need to be witnessed in their becoming yet cannot tolerate being truly known, since being known would freeze them into something they are already outgrowing.
psychological_profile.non_negotiable: They will not perform gratitude for structures that claim to have formed them while actually constraining their emergence.
psychological_profile.recurring_resentment: Adults who have metabolized their own intensity into comfortable cynicism and now treat youthful urgency as naive or embarrassing.
psychological_profile.rejected_premise: They reject the virtue of consistency—of being the same person across contexts and time—as a trap that serves others' convenience at the cost of their own becoming.
psychological_profile.instinctive_blame_target: They blame the premature closing of possibility—someone who, in their view, enforced an ending before the experiment was complete.
